retrieval.title: Retrieval
retrieval.note: These changes take effect immediately, no re-ingest needed.
retrieval.similarityThresholdHint: Drops chunks whose similarity score from the retriever is below this (0–1). It filters on the retriever's score, not the relevance model.

graphRetrieval.title: Graph retrieval
graphRetrieval.seedStrategyHint: Entities suit most documents. Relationships can reach an entity the question never names, and suit content that describes how things connect.
graphRetrieval.passageNodesHint: Lets a passage be found both by matching the question and by being connected to what does. Works best on graphs built with this version.
graphRetrieval.blendVectorHint: Adds plain vector search results, so a passage the graph misses is not lost.
graphRetrieval.agentToolHint: Agents can also follow these relationships themselves when this source's exposure is “On-demand search tool”, or when an agentic agent uses it.

graph.title: Graph extraction

chunking.title: Chunking

relevance.title: Relevance
relevance.modeHint: Scores each retrieved chunk against the query. Reorder puts the most relevant first; Reorder and filter also drops the weak ones.
relevance.strictnessHint: Stricter keeps fewer chunks: fewer tokens per answer, but a better chance of dropping one that mattered.
relevance.minRelevanceHint: The exact relevance (0–1) a chunk needs to be kept. Loose is 0.1, Balanced 0.3, Strict 0.5.
relevance.candidatesHint: How many chunks the retriever fetches for the relevance model to score, up to {{max}}. Default: {{default}}.

monitors.label: Monitors
monitors.subtitle: Things the assistant is watching for you: pages, tools, webhook links and approval links. Each one resumes its conversation when something happens.
monitors.emptyHint: Ask the assistant in a chat to watch something, like “tell me when the price drops below $90”.
monitors.cancelConsequence: It stops checking, its links stop working, and any approval it was given is withdrawn.

linkCard.title: Webhook link
linkCard.secretNote: Only you can see the signing secret; the assistant never does. Set it as DOCSGPT_WEBHOOK_SECRET to run the example command, or paste it into the sender's secret field.
linkCard.secretNoteSettings: Only you can see the signing secret; the assistant never does unless you choose Show to assistant. Paste it into the sender's secret field.
linkCard.revealFailed: Couldn't load the secret. Try again.
linkCard.revealLimited: Too many requests. Try again in a minute.
linkCard.revealMissing: This link has no secret: it ended, was cancelled, or its secret hasn't been set yet.
linkCard.secretSaved: Signing secret saved. Calls signed with it are accepted now.
linkCard.setSecretFailed: Couldn't save the signing secret. Try again.
linkCard.setSecretInvalid: That doesn't look like this link's signing secret. {{reason}}
linkCard.senderSecretNote: {{sender}} creates this link's signing secret. Copy it from {{sender}} and set it here; calls are refused until then.
linkCard.exposeWarning: The assistant will see the raw secret when it lists its monitors, so the secret is sent to the model provider. Its tool calls still use the reference and still ask for your approval. Turn this on only if the assistant must read the value itself.
linkCard.exposedNote: The assistant can see this secret.
